sections.title: Overview of Environmental Health Safety
sections.text:
8.1 Overview of Environmental Health Safety
EHS is a broad term to describe the laws, rules, regulations, professions,
programs, and workplace efforts that aim to protect the health and safety of
employees and the public, as well as the environment, from hazards associated
with the workplace. Essentially, EHS encompasses the profession of
occupational safety and health professionals, along with their colleagues in the
environmental department.
EHS is a discipline that focuses on protecting the health and safety of people, as
well as preserving the natural environment. The primary objective of EHS is to
prevent accidents, injuries, and illnesses in the workplace, while minimizing the
impact of business operations on the environment.
The roles and functions of EHS professionals may vary depending on the
organization and industry, but typically include the following:
Developing and implementing safety policies and procedures: EHS
professionals are responsible for developing and enforcing safety policies and
procedures to ensure compliance with regulations and standards.
Conducting safety training and education: EHS professionals provide safety
training to employees to ensure they have the knowledge and skills to work
safely and prevent accidents.
Conducting safety inspections and audits: EHS professionals conduct safety
inspections and audits to identify hazards and risks and recommend
corrective actions.
Investigating accidents and incidents: EHS professionals investigate accidents
and incidents to determine their root causes and to recommend corrective
actions and prevent similar incidents in the future.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

462
Managing hazardous materials and waste: EHS professionals manage
hazardous materials and waste to ensure they are handled, stored, and
disposed of safely and in compliance with regulations.
Developing and implementing environmental programs: EHS professionals
develop and implement programs to manage environmental risks, such as air
and water pollution, waste management, and energy conservation.
Overall, the role of EHS professionals is to ensure the safety and well-being of
employees, protect the environment, and maintain regulatory compliance in the
workplace. In another words, EHS is a discipline that focuses on implementing
practical measures to protect the environment and ensure health and safety in
the workplace. From a safety standpoint, it involves creating organized
procedures to identify workplace hazards and reduce accidents and exposure to
harmful situations and substances. Additionally, personnel are trained in
accident prevention, emergency preparedness, and the use of protective
clothing and equipment.
At its core, EHS aims to develop safe, high-quality, and environmentally friendly
processes, working practices, and systemic activities that prevent or reduce the
risk of harm to people in general, to operators, or to patients. From an
environmental standpoint, EHS involves implementing a systematic approach to
comply with regulations regarding waste management, air emissions, and
reducing a site’s carbon footprint.
Regulatory requirements are essential in the EHS discipline, and EHS managers
must identify and understand relevant regulations, communicating their
implications to executive management so that the company can implement
appropriate measures. In the United States, organizations are subject to EHS
regulations outlined in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), particularly CFR
29, 40, and 49. However, EHS management is not limited to legal compliance,
and companies are encouraged to go beyond what is required by law as
appropriate.
SAP EHS Management is a software solution provided by SAP designed to help
organizations manage their EHS risks and compliance requirements. This
integrated solution allows organizations to manage their EHS data, processes,
and reporting in a single system.
SAP EHS Management works by providing a range of modules that allow
organizations to manage their EHS data and processes. These modules include:
© 

463
Product safety
This module allows organizations to manage the safety of their products by
tracking and reporting on hazardous substances, chemical compliance, and
labeling requirements.
Dangerous goods management
This module allows organizations to manage the transportation and storage
of hazardous materials in compliance with local and international
regulations.
Waste management
This module allows organizations to manage their waste management
processes, including waste generation, storage, and disposal.
Occupational health
This module allows organizations to manage the health and safety of their
employees, including monitoring and reporting on workplace hazards and
incidents.
Industrial hygiene and safety
This module allows organizations to manage their industrial hygiene and
safety processes, including risk assessments, inspections, and audits.
Environ ment
This module allows organizations to manage their environmental compliance
requirements, including air and water quality monitoring, emissions
reporting, and sustainability reporting.
SAP EHS Management provides various features that assist organizations in
maintaining employee health and safety, product and reach compliance,
product safety, and environmental compliance management, including the
following:
Employee health and safety
This functionality deals with processes related to industrial hygiene and
occupational health to ensure the well-being of workers and the workplace.
When workers handle dangerous substances, they must follow specific
guidelines, and SAP EHS Management simplifies this process. Additionally, it
incorporates risk management and asset management processes and places
risk data into work orders, along with proposing safety measures.
Product and reach compliance
This functionality helps organizations maintain records of materials and
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

464
products while upholding compliance regulations for their industries. It
establishes compliance workflows, and authorities can assign guidelines and
legal necessities to business operations, ensuring the safety of production
materials and final products.
Product safety
This functionality helps organizations meet their legal, safety, and
sustainability responsibilities while maintaining the supply chain of products.
It also maintains regulations for product storage, packaging, and
transportation.
Environmental compliance management
This functionality maintains different environmental laws and regulations,
allowing organizations to track air and water emissions records to ensure
environmental safety. All environment-related activities and tasks can be
tracked using this feature of SAP EHS Management.
SAP EHS Management provides numerous benefits, including the following
capabilities:
Maintaining industrial hygiene and occupational health programs
Analyzing operational data to anticipate hazards and taking steps to reduce
them
Sharing data, integrating business processes, and sharing workflows to
strengthen the EHS process
Safeguarding operational continuity by identifying and moderating safety
risks
Assisting organizations in following legal and safety guidelines, thus
preventing accidental expenses
Enhancing the safety norms of business operations
Analyzing accidents efficiently to avoid them in the future
Incorporating risk management strategies into daily business activities, thus
reducing the chances of risk and creating awareness among workers
Creating and implementing health surveillance agreements
Preparing surveys and tasks to collect information about working
environment conditions
© 

465
SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM are two different modules within an SAP
system. The integration of these two modules allows for a more efficient and
streamlined management of hazardous materials and other related processes.
The integration of SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM involves several key
steps, including:
1. Configuring the necessary settings in both SAP EHS Management and SAP
EWM: This step involves setting up the relevant organizational structures,
material master data, and other necessary master data in both modules.
2. Defining EHS-related classes for hazardous materials in SAP EWM: These
classes are used to identify and manage hazardous materials in the
warehouse and transportation processes.
3. Replicating master data between SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM: This
step involves setting up the interfaces and data transfer mechanisms
between the two modules, allowing for the exchange of data such as
material safety data sheets (MSDS), product safety data sheets (PSDS), and
other relevant data.
4. Setting up safety stock and inventory management in SAP EWM: This step
ensures that the required safety stock levels are maintained for hazardous
materials and that inventory levels are accurately tracked and managed.
5. Executing EHS-related functions within SAP EWM: This step includes
handling hazardous materials, waste disposal, and other related processes
within a warehouse.
Overall, the integration of SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM provides a
comprehensive solution for managing hazardous materials, ensuring
compliance with safety regulations and reducing the risk of accidents and
incidents in the warehouse and transportation processes

8.2 Goods Receipt and Goods Issue Process Using
SAP EHS Management
In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the goods receipt and
goods issue process using SAP EHS Management. We’ll begin with the inbound
process. For both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process,
configuration, and master data setup needed and then provide a process
demonstration.

sections.title: Inbound Process
sections.text:
8.2.1 Inbound Process
In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the inbound goods receipt process using
SAP EHS Management by utilizing embedded EWM. This section is divided into
four parts: inbound goods receipt business process, configuration needed for
the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 8.1, an inbound process in SAP EWM involves the receiving
and storage of goods in a warehouse or distribution center. The business process
for the receipt and putaway of hazardous material is involves the following
steps:
1. A purchase order for hazardous materials is generated in SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA. The purchase order triggers the automatic creation of an inbound
delivery, which is then replicated to SAP EWM in the background.
2. When the material is physically received in the warehouse, the warehouse
team generates a warehouse task and physically places the material in the
hazardous storage area in the SAP EWM system. A putaway strategy is
defined for hazardous materials, guiding warehouse operators to physically
store the material in the designated hazardous area and confirm the
warehouse task accordingly.
3. After the material is stored in the hazardous area, the warehouse team
performs a goods receipt in SAP EWM, which generates inventory in both
the SAP EWM and SAP S/4HANA systems.
© 

467
Figure 8.1 Inbound Process Using SAP EHS Management
Configuration
In this section, we’ll cover the key customization steps required for this process,
assuming that the main SAP EWM customization settings have already been
configured in the system:
1. Define a storage type for storing hazardous material
This configuration setting is needed to store hazardous material in
designated storage area. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended
Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master
Data • Define Storage Types. To define a storage type for hazardous
material, on the Change View “Define Storage Types”: Details screen,
click New Entries. For the Hazard.Sub.Mgmt field, make sure the value
selected is 2 - Haz.sub.check at stor.type and stor.section levels or verify
these settings meet your business requirements, as shown in Figure 8.2.
Figure 8.2 Define Storage Type

468

In this configuration setting, storage sections will be defined. Follow the IMG
menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended

New Entries in the Change View “Define Storage Sections”: Overview
screen and create the storage section, as shown in Figure 8.3.
Figure 8.3 Define Storage Section

This represents a tailored solution in accordance with specific business

Process Demo
In this section, we’ll go through an inbound process using SAP EHS Management
step by step:

1. Create a purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To create a purchase order, execute Transaction ME21N. Input the supplier,
material, purchase order quantity, plant, and receiving storage location and

Figure 8.19 Create a Purchase Order

Figure 8.21 Display an Inbound Delivery

8.2.2 Outbound Process
In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the outbound goods issue process using
SAP EHS Management by utilizing embedded EWM. This section is divided into
four parts: business process, configuration needed for the process, master data,
and step-by-step process flow.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 8.27, an outbound process with SAP EWM and SAP EHS
Management involves the following steps:
1. The outbound process typically starts in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when a
sales order is created. An outbound delivery is created in SAP ERP or SAP
S/4HANA with reference to the sales order, This outbound delivery is
automatically is replicated in SAP EWM for further processing.
2. In SAP EWM, a wave is created for the outbound delivery order. Upon wave
release, a warehouse task to pick the hazardous material is automatically
created and is based on the picking strategy for the hazardous material.
3. Hazardous material is further picked, packed, and loaded as per the
warehouse process. Once the process is complete, the warehouse team
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

480
performs the goods issue for the outbound delivery order, and the
outbound process is completed.
Figure 8.27 Outbound Process Using SAP EHS Management
Configuration
In this section, we’ll go through the important configuration steps needed for
outbound processes using SAP EHS Management:
1. Define storage type search sequence
This configuration setting is needed to specify the storage type search
sequence. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse
Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Issue Process
• Strategies • Specify Storage Type Search Sequence. Click New Entries
and maintain warehouse and storage type to specify the stock removal
indicator, as shown in Figure 8.28.
Figure 8.28 Define Storage Type Search Sequence
2. Determine the storage type search sequence for stock removal
This configuration setting determines the storage type search sequence for
stock removal. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse
Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Issue Process
• Strategies • Determine Storage Type Search Sequence for Stock
Removal. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse, Stock Removal
© 

481

HazRat2 (hazardous rating 2), Storage Type, and RemR (stock removal
rule) fields, as shown in Figure 8.29.
Figure 8.29 Determine Storage Type Search Sequence for Stock Removal
Master Data Setup
Only one master data step is required for this process: maintaining the pick
control indicator in SAP EWM. To maintain this indicator for the product master,
follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse
Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Product •
Maintain Warehouse Product or execute Transaction /SCWM/MAT1. Click the
Warehouse tab and maintain the Storage Removal Indicator field, as shown in
Figure 8.30.
Figure 8.30 Display Warehouse Product

In this section, we’ll go through the outbound process using SAP EHS

1. Initiate a customer sales order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To a create sales order, execute Transaction VA01. Enter Order type and
Sales area details. Click Continue and, on the next screen, enter all the

To display the outbound delivery in SAP EWM, execute Transaction

5. Confirm the pick warehouse task for hazardous material in SAP EWM

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
8.3 Summary
That’s it! You’re now prepared to work on EHS processes in your own company.
In this chapter, we provided an overview of EHS in general and explored the
benefits of SAP EHS Management specifically. Additionally, we delved into the
available deployment options for integrating SAP EHS Management with SAP
EWM and SAP ERP. Furthermore, we covered inbound and outbound processes
using the integration of SAP EWM, SAP EHS Management, and either SAP ERP or
SAP S/4HANA.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

486
9 Plant Maintenance
Plant maintenance is a sophisticated module incorporated within the SAP’s
enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, specifically designed to assist
organizations in effectively managing and up keeping their plants,
equipment, and assets. Its purpose is to optimize maintenance procedures,
minimize downtime, and enhance overall operational efficiency. By utilizing
plant maintenance, your company can bolster asset reliability, reduce
maintenance costs, and elevate its overall operational effectiveness. The
primary objective of this chapter is to furnish you with a comprehensive
understanding of plant maintenance.
Plant maintenance is an integral part of SAP ERP helps enterprises manage and
preserve their equipment and systems. The plant maintenance application
component is a comprehensive tool to streamline maintenance activities. With
plant maintenance, an organization can automate repairs and optimize
maintenance requests. This application allows users to document issues within
the SAP system, plan labor and material activities, and track and settle costs.
The integration of SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) with plant
maintenance is crucial for optimizing the handling of goods in the maintenance
process. By integrating these two systems, an organization can ensure efficient
coordination between warehouse operations and maintenance activities.
This chapter begins with an overview of plant maintenance, highlighting its key
benefits and the advantages of integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM. We
also cover various scenarios and functionalities related to plant maintenance-
SAP EWM integration, specifically focusing on outbound processes and return
(inbound) processes using plant maintenance orders. This chapter provides
detailed information about the business processes, configuration, and master
data and offers an end-to-end demonstration of the entire process.
Emphasis will be placed on plant maintenance, which is an SAP system
meticulously tailored to cater to the requirements of maintaining your plants.
The central focus of this chapter is on providing an overview of plant
maintenance and elucidating the various involved processes. We will offer
meticulous insights into the plant maintenance process, coupled with a step-by-
©
